claim_types.name: Accident or Collision
claim_types.short_desc: For vehicle collisions, roadside accidents, or physical damage involving another vehicle or stationary object.
claim_types.guidance: File the claim as early as possible after the incident. Avoid moving the vehicle before taking clear photos unless required for road safety.

documents.name: Duly Signed Claim Form
documents.description: The official insurance claim application providing details of when, where, and how the accident occurred.
documents.tip: Ensure the signature matches the policyholder's signature on the original policy schedule.

documents.name: Insurance Policy Certificate / Schedule
documents.description: Proof of active coverage showing policy number, validity dates, Insured Declared Value (IDV), and coverage terms.
documents.tip: Verify that the accident occurred within the active validity window.

documents.name: Vehicle Registration Certificate (RC)
documents.description: Verifies legal ownership, vehicle chassis number, engine number, and registration credentials.
documents.tip: Ensure registration is active and the vehicle type matches the insured category.

documents.name: Driver's Licence (DL) of Person Driving
documents.description: Proof that the individual operating the vehicle at the time of the collision held a valid driving permit.
documents.tip: The license must be valid for the specific vehicle category (e.g., LMV / Non-Transport).

documents.name: Photographs & Video of Vehicle Damage
documents.description: Clear photographic evidence showing point of impact, wide angle of accident spot, and visible damages.
documents.tip: Take close-ups and wide shots showing the vehicle's registration plate and odometer reading.

documents.name: Repair Estimate & Garage Work Order
documents.description: An itemized cost breakdown of parts replacement and labor required to restore the vehicle.
documents.tip: Do not authorize repairs before the insurer's surveyor inspects the vehicle.

documents.name: Police FIR / Accident Report (If Applicable)
documents.description: Mandatory if third-party injury, death, major property damage, or dispute over accident liability occurred.
documents.tip: Often waived by insurers for minor collisions without third-party bodily injury.

documents.name: Medical Records / Hospital Bills (If Injured)
documents.description: Required if claiming personal accident coverage for medical expenses or driver injuries.
documents.tip: Keep original discharge summaries, prescriptions, and payment receipts.

claim_types.name: Vehicle Theft / Total Loss
claim_types.short_desc: For vehicle stolen from parking, robbery, or unauthorized seizure resulting in total loss.
claim_types.guidance: Report theft to the police immediately (within 24 hours) and notify your insurer right away. Prompt reporting is critical for theft claims.

documents.name: Signed Theft Claim Application Form
documents.description: Formal claim declaration detailing the exact time, location, circumstances of theft, and last seen condition.
documents.tip: State facts accurately; discrepancies between police statement and claim form cause delays.

documents.name: Police First Information Report (FIR)
documents.description: Certified copy of the criminal FIR filed immediately following the theft under section 379/theft law.
documents.tip: Get a certified/stamped copy from the police station where the complaint was lodged.

documents.name: All Original Vehicle Keys (Both sets)
documents.description: Surrender of both original factory keys as physical proof the vehicle was not left unattended with keys.
documents.tip: If a duplicate key was lost earlier, submit the written declaration made at the time.

documents.name: Original Registration Certificate (RC Book)
documents.description: Original registration card surrendered to the insurer along with Form 28, 29, and 30 for title transfer.
documents.tip: Ensure all outstanding road taxes and hypothecations are cleared.

documents.name: Police Final Untraced Report / Non-Traceable Certificate
documents.description: Final court-accepted certificate declaring that law enforcement could not locate or recover the stolen vehicle.
documents.tip: Usually issued 60 to 90 days after the FIR is filed if the vehicle remains untraceable.

documents.name: RTO Theft Intimation & Non-Use Letter
documents.description: Official letter intimating the RTO that the vehicle is stolen and blacklisting the registration against misuse.
documents.tip: Obtain an acknowledgment stamp from the RTO office.

documents.name: NOC & Form 35 from Financier (If Financed)
documents.description: No Objection Certificate and loan clearance or foreclosure statement if the car was bought on loan.
documents.tip: Claim payout is routed through the financier until loan is satisfied.

claim_types.name: Vehicle Damage (Non-Collision / Weather / Fire)
claim_types.short_desc: For damages caused by natural calamities (floods, storms, hail), fire, self-ignition, vandalism, or falling objects.
claim_types.guidance: Do not attempt to crank or start a flood-submerged engine, as hydrostatic lock may void engine protector coverage.

documents.name: Completed Claim Form with Incident Details
documents.description: Specifies cause of damage (e.g. tree branch fell during gale storm, flood water inundation, garage fire).
documents.tip: Provide clear timeline and environmental context of the damage event.

documents.name: High-Resolution Incident & Damage Photos
documents.description: Photos showing the vehicle in its damaged state at the spot, water level marks, or charred areas.
documents.tip: Capture context photos showing surrounding environment (fallen tree, flooded street, fire aftermath).

documents.name: Copy of Vehicle RC & Active Policy Schedule
documents.description: Verifies valid comprehensive (Own Damage) insurance coverage and legal vehicle ownership.
documents.tip: Third-Party-only (TPO) policies do not cover natural disaster or own damage.

documents.name: Fire Brigade Report (For Fire Incidents)
documents.description: Official incident summary report from the fire emergency services confirming fire call and cause.
documents.tip: Required whenever external fire department intervention occurred.

documents.name: Meteorological Report / Media Report (Flood/Storm)
documents.description: Newspaper clippings or government alerts verifying widespread flooding, cyclone, or severe weather.
documents.tip: Helps expedite claims during catastrophic weather events declared by authorities.

documents.name: Towing Service Receipt & Bill
documents.description: Receipt for transporting the immobilized vehicle from incident location to the authorized workshop.
documents.tip: Check if your policy includes Roadside Assistance or towing expense reimbursement limit.
